body.statement:
For every fixed finite \((\mathcal W,\mathcal Z)\), there is a one-copy structural compiler \(\mathscr A\) with the following properties.  It rejects a cell rank exceeding two.  Every rank-two cell is represented by its two oriented segment modes, refined by all coefficient support faces.  Every rank-one cell is represented by the disjoint \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm E,\mathrm D\) modes of \(\mathrm{lem:rank\text{-}one\text{-}lred\text{-}normal\text{-}forms}\), with the \(\mathrm E\) split refined coordinatewise.  Products of the four local modes use one shared variable \(b_i\) at each response vertex and are refined by proxy supports, endpoint equalities and inequalities, observed-line incidences, and nonzero pivots.  Writing \(X_\chi\) for a resulting chart and \(X=\bigcup_\chi X_\chi\), the union is exactly \(\mathcal C_A(T)\).  In design B, adjoining \(\rho\), the zero-residual or active negatively proportional state at every response type, lexicographic nonzero pivots, forest propagation, the active-cycle product-one equation, positive component scales, normalization, and a signed relevance witness gives a finite chart union equal exactly to \(\mathcal C_B(T)\).

The compiler tests every \(X_\chi\) for emptiness.  If the union is nonempty, exact one-copy sampling supplies \(x_0\in X\), and the compiler sets \(t_0=\tau_C(x_0)\).  It then tests, separately for every chart,
\[
 V_\chi(t_0)=\left\{x\in X_\chi:
 \bigl(\tau_{C,1}(x)-t_{0,1}\bigr)^2+
 \bigl(\tau_{C,2}(x)-t_{0,2}\bigr)^2>0\right\}.             \tag{18}
\]
The target image \(\tau_C(X)\) is a singleton if and only if every set in (18) is empty.  A nonempty refinement directly supplies a sampled \(x_1\) with \(\tau_C(x_1)\ne t_0\), and the two cycle points lift to legal target-changing full SCMs.  Thus the decision uses one sampled feasible point and one-copy existential realizability on each structural chart; it uses neither connected-component enumeration nor target projection, although either may be computed as an optional diagnostic.

Over an arbitrary real input field \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), the calculation is relative to effective field arithmetic, order, sign-determination, and real-root oracles.  The tests in (18) are performed over the ordered finite extension \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_{0,1},t_{0,2})\).  A rigid value is returned as a rational expression in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) only when that expression is constructed; otherwise it is returned by a real-univariate representation and Thom data over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).
body.justification: The theorem proves the exhaustive structural chart union and the globally complete one-sample disagreement test.
body.gap: The previous evaluator unnecessarily decomposed charts into connected components and projected the target.
body.consumer: All downstream procedures obtain compatibility, an exact common target, or legal target-changing witnesses from one-copy chart realizability.
body.proof_tex:
We first prove that the structural charts are exhaustive, independently of the target test.  By \(\mathrm{ass:selected\text{-}table\text{-}positivity}\), each entry of \(T_e\) and every \(v_e(z)\) is positive.  In any cycle factorization with \(\mathcal I_e=\{i,j\}\),
\[
 T_e=b_i a_{ei}^{\top}+b_j a_{ej}^{\top},
 \qquad a_{ei}(z)+a_{ej}(z)=v_e(z).                         \tag{19}
\]
The right side of (19) has rank at most two.  Hence a rank exceeding two makes the chart union and the cycle fiber empty, while positivity excludes rank zero.

Suppose first that \(\operatorname{rank}(T_e)=2\).  Define the observable normalized columns
\[
 c_{ez}=\frac{T_e(\mathord\cdot,z)}{v_e(z)}.
\]
Equation (19) gives
\[
 c_{ez}=\lambda_{ez}b_i+(1-\lambda_{ez})b_j,
 \qquad \lambda_{ez}=\frac{a_{ei}(z)}{v_e(z)}\in[0,1].       \tag{20}
\]
Rank two forces \(b_i\ne b_j\) and at least two distinct values of \(\lambda_{ez}\); consequently the affine hull of the observed \(c_{ez}\)'s is the line through \(b_i,b_j\).  Thus all observed columns lie in the closed segment \([b_i,b_j]\).  Conversely, if distinct simplex points \(b_i,b_j\) lie on that observed line and their segment contains every \(c_{ez}\), choose a coordinate \(h_e\) with \(b_i(h_e)\ne b_j(h_e)\) and put
\[
 a_{ei}(z)=v_e(z)
 \frac{c_{ez}(h_e)-b_j(h_e)}{b_i(h_e)-b_j(h_e)},
 \qquad
 a_{ej}(z)=v_e(z)-a_{ei}(z).                               \tag{21}
\]
Containment makes both coefficients nonnegative; (21) and the affine-line identity recover every column of \(T_e\), so (19) holds.  The two endpoint orders in \(\mathrm{thm:rank\text{-}two\text{-}orientation\text{-}atlas}\) exhaust the possibilities.  At each \(z\), positivity of \(v_e(z)\) leaves exactly three support states: \(a_{ei}(z)=0\), \(a_{ej}(z)=0\), or both are positive.  Their coordinatewise refinements therefore exhaust every rank-two support face.

If \(\operatorname{rank}(T_e)=1\), \(\mathrm{lem:rank\text{-}one\text{-}lred\text{-}normal\text{-}forms}\) proves that exactly one of the \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm E,\mathrm D\) modes holds.  In particular, modes \(\mathrm L\) and \(\mathrm R\) retain the inactive endpoint as a free simplex point subject only to its other incident cell, while mode \(\mathrm E\) retains the entire vector split \(s_e\).  The three coordinatewise alternatives \(s_e(z)=0\), \(0<s_e(z)<v_e(z)\), and \(s_e(z)=v_e(z)\) exhaust its boundary faces.

Take the product of the four local lists and use one variable \(b_i\) for the two cells incident to response type \(i\).  Refine proxy supports, endpoint equalities and inequalities, observed-line incidences, coefficient supports, and each guarded pivot by their finitely many sign alternatives.  Formula (21) and the rank-one normal-form lemma place every point of \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) in at least one such chart.  Conversely, direct substitution of the chart equations into (19), together with the simplex and nonnegativity atoms, places every chart point in \(\mathcal C_A(T)\).  Therefore
\[
 \mathcal C_A(T)=\bigcup_\chi X_\chi .                    \tag{22}
\]
This equality includes coincident endpoints, inactive rows, simultaneous rank-one cells, and forced-zero incident coefficients.

For design B, fix a chart in (22) and a positive projective vector \(\rho\).  By \(\mathrm{thm:iv\text{-}residual\text{-}forest}\), the two residuals incident to a response type must either both vanish or be nonzero and negatively proportional; a branch with exactly one zero residual is empty.  In an active branch, the lexicographically first nonzero coordinate and its sign give a finite pivot list and determine a positive ratio of incident margins.  The active subgraph of the response four-cycle is a forest unless all four links are active.  On a forest, ratios propagate from one positive scale per connected component.  When the whole cycle is active, propagation is consistent exactly when the product of the four oriented ratios equals one.  Positive scales and the single margin normalization give all and only the positive solutions.  Finally, the finite alternatives
\[
 q^X_zg(z')-q^X_{z'}g(z)>0
 \quad\hbox{or}\quad
 q^X_zg(z')-q^X_{z'}g(z)<0,
 \qquad z<z',                                               \tag{23}
\]
are exhaustive for relevance.  The cited residual-forest theorem now proves that the refined union is exactly \(\mathcal C_B(T)\).

Each \(X_\chi\) is a one-copy semialgebraic set over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\): every denominator cleared in constructing it is either a positive observed margin or a pivot whose nonzero sign is an atom of that chart.  The sampling and realizability algorithms in \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}real\text{-}algebraic\text{-}sampling\text{-}and\text{-}existential}\) therefore decide every chart's emptiness and return a real-univariate sample from any nonempty chart.  If all charts are empty, (22) and its design-B analogue prove incompatibility.  Otherwise choose one returned point \(x_0\), put \(t_0=\tau_C(x_0)\), and represent the ordered field \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_{0,1},t_{0,2})\) by the cited primitive-element and Thom algorithms.  Because \(\tau_C\) is linear in the incident coefficient vectors, (18) adds one polynomial strict inequality of degree two and no new latent copy.  The cited existential algorithm decides each \(V_\chi(t_0)\) and samples it when nonempty.

If every \(V_\chi(t_0)\) is empty, then for arbitrary \(x\in X\) there is a chart \(X_\chi\) containing \(x\).  Its refinement is empty, so the nonnegative squared distance in (18) equals zero and \(\tau_C(x)=t_0\).  Hence \(\tau_C(X)=\{t_0\}\).  Conversely, if \(\tau_C(X)=\{t_0\}\), the strict inequality in (18) is false at every chart point, so every refinement is empty.  This proves the claimed equivalence without a connected-component decomposition.

As an exact smallest-face check, take every endpoint \(b_i\) equal to the uniform distribution on \(\mathcal W\) and every \(T_e\) equal to the product of that endpoint with the uniform \(v_e\) on \(\mathcal Z\).  Put every rank-one cell in mode \(\mathrm E\).  One legal cycle point uses each split \(s_e=v_e/2\).  For any rational \(0<\delta<1/2\), a second legal point replaces only
\[
 a_{11,2}=\left(\frac12+\delta\right)v_{11},
 \qquad
 a_{11,1}=\left(\frac12-\delta\right)v_{11}.
\]
All coefficients remain positive, every observed cell table is unchanged, and the first target coordinate changes from \(1/2\) to \(1/2+\delta\).  Thus the relevant set in (18) is nonempty on this coincident-endpoint support face, exactly as the global criterion declares.

If some \(V_\chi(t_0)\) is nonempty, its sampled point \(x_1\) satisfies \(\tau_C(x_1)\ne\tau_C(x_0)\) by (18).  The exact structural union makes both points legal cycle points, and \(\mathrm{lem:cycle\text{-}to\text{-}scm\text{-}lift}\) supplies two full SCMs with identical observables and, in design A, identical supplied margins.  If all refinements are empty, the sample representation of \(x_0\) supplies exact rational coordinate functions for \(t_0\) in one real algebraic primitive element.  The compiler emits a field expression only if exact arithmetic constructs one in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\); otherwise it retains the square-free real-univariate and Thom representation.  All branching predicates have coefficients generated by the observable input and the exactly represented \(t_0\), so the resulting compatibility and agreement certificates are observable.
